idiom_name: json-rules-engine: JSON conditions over facts, events on match
implementation_notes: json-rules-engine stores rules as JSON: a condition tree of all/any/not nodes over {fact, operator, value} leaves plus a single event to emit when it matches. Facts are passed to engine.run(facts) or registered with addFact (async providers are resolved once per run and cached), operators are extensible, and no eval() is used - conditions are interpreted, which is what makes the rule set portable data that can be persisted and reloaded. It is the pragmatic JavaScript answer when rules are edited outside the app: keep the JSON in a store, validate it against a schema, and treat it as a versioned artifact.
pitfalls: Undefined facts throw unless allowUndefinedFacts is enabled - and enabling it turns a renamed fact into a silently false condition, so fact names need contract tests.
Rules are unvalidated data: nothing checks operator names or value shapes, so a rule store needs schema validation and a replay suite before it is trusted.
Async fact providers are cached per run: rule logic that reads a fact after mutating its source sees a stale value.
Priority sets evaluation order, not exclusivity: overlapping rules all emit their events unless the caller deactivates them.

variants.name: Array of when/then closures
variants.idiom_name: array of {name, when, then} arrow functions over a facts object
variants.implementation_notes: The zero-dependency JavaScript form is a rule array: each rule is a condition function and an action function over a plain facts object, evaluated in a loop in declared order. Arrow functions and array methods are all that is needed; rules stay inside the bundle, so they are unit-tested and refactored like code, and there is no engine, agenda or schema to learn. Use it until rules must be editable without a deploy - at that point a declarative JSON engine pays for itself.
pitfalls: Rule order is control flow: overlapping conditions fire in array order with no conflict resolution, so precedence must be modelled explicitly or the rules made disjoint.
Functions are not data: the rule set cannot be shipped to a client or edited without a build - the exact problem the declarative variant solves.
Actions that mutate the facts under their own condition re-trigger on the next pass unless a fired flag or a bounded loop stops them.
